Profile One or More Documents with Caller-Supplied Lexical Norms

lexdiv_norm_profile.Rd

Computes token- and/or type-weighted arithmetic means for one or more lexical-norm variables on one document or a multi-document corpus from matched observed keys while reporting resource and annotation coverage separately.

Usage

lexdiv_norm_profile(
  x,
  norms,
  key,
  measure_specs = NULL,
  resource = lexdiv_resource_meta("caller_norms"),
  weightings = c("token", "type"),
  id_col = "document_id",
  term_col = "terms",
  max_rows = 1e+06
)

lexdiv_norm_spec(
  value_column,
  measure_id = NULL,
  construct_id = measure_id,
  value_unit = "unspecified",
  direction = "descriptive",
  language = "unspecified",
  variety = "unspecified",
  population_id = "unspecified",
  collection_year = "unspecified",
  valid_min = NA_real_,
  valid_max = NA_real_
)

lexdiv_resource_meta(
  resource_id = "caller_resource",
  resource_version = "unspecified",
  creator = "unspecified",
  source_reference = "unspecified",
  data_license = "unspecified",
  transformation_id = "none",
  lookup_unit = "exact_term",
  resource_key_normalization_id = "caller-prepared-v1"
)

# S3 method for class 'lexdiv_norm_profile'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lexdiv_norm_profile_batch'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

x

For a single document, a character vector of caller-prepared lookup terms or a lexdiv_tokenization object. For multiple documents, a named list of term vectors, a lexdiv_tokenization_batch object, or a data frame/tibble with id_col and term_col. For print(), a lexdiv_norm_profile or lexdiv_norm_profile_batch object.

norms

A data frame or tibble containing one unique key column and numeric norm columns. Non-numeric metadata columns are ignored automatically when measure_specs = NULL.

key

One string naming the exact-match key column in norms.

measure_specs

Optional data frame or tibble of 11 measure-specification columns (from lexdiv_norm_spec()). When NULL, defaults to all plain numeric columns in norms other than key, sanitizing non-identifier column names (such as "%_known" to "pct_known").

resource

Named list of 8 resource-metadata fields from lexdiv_resource_meta().

weightings

A non-empty subset of c("token", "type").

id_col

Document-ID column name for multi-document data-frame input.

term_col

Term list-column name for multi-document data-frame input (default "terms"), or token column name for tokenization input (defaults to "surface" when omitted).

max_rows

Positive whole-number row bound checked before allocation.

value_column, measure_id, construct_id, value_unit, direction, language, variety, population_id, collection_year, valid_min, valid_max

Vectorized or scalar fields recycled across value_column by lexdiv_norm_spec().

resource_id, resource_version, creator, source_reference, data_license, transformation_id, lookup_unit, resource_key_normalization_id

Scalar provenance fields assembled by lexdiv_resource_meta().

...

Additional arguments passed to print.data.frame().

Value

For a single document, lexdiv_norm_profile() returns a lexdiv_norm_profile list with status, summary, lookup, coverage, provenance, and diagnostics. For multiple documents, it returns a lexdiv_norm_profile_batch list with document-major summary, lookup, and coverage tables. lexdiv_norm_spec() returns an 11-column specification data frame. lexdiv_resource_meta() returns an 8-element metadata list. print() returns x invisibly.

See also

nj8_profile, tubelex_profile

Examples

norms <- data.frame(
  term = c("book", "read", "rare"),
  familiarity = c(6, 5, NA_real_),
  aoa = c(4.2, 5.0, 11.5),
  note = c("noun", "verb", "adj")
)

# Single document (non-numeric 'note' column is ignored automatically):
quick <- lexdiv_norm_profile(c("book", "book", "rare", "unknown"), norms, "term")
quick
#> <lexdiv_norm_profile: ok; caller_norms@unspecified; 2 measures; 8 lookup rows; schema 0.1.0>
#>   measure_id weighting estimate status missing_reason resource_coverage
#>  familiarity     token 6.000000     ok           <NA>         0.7500000
#>  familiarity      type 6.000000     ok           <NA>         0.6666667
#>          aoa     token 6.633333     ok           <NA>         0.7500000
#>          aoa      type 7.850000     ok           <NA>         0.6666667
#>  annotation_coverage
#>            0.6666667
#>            0.5000000
#>            1.0000000
#>            1.0000000
#> Means are conditional on observed matched values; inspect $coverage.

# Multiple documents with explicit metadata:
specs <- lexdiv_norm_spec(
  c("familiarity", "aoa"),
  direction = c("higher", "lower"),
  valid_min = c(1, 0),
  valid_max = c(7, 25)
)
meta <- lexdiv_resource_meta("example_norms", resource_version = "2025-01")
batch <- lexdiv_norm_profile(
  list(d1 = c("book", "read"), d2 = c("rare", "unknown")),
  norms, "term", specs, meta
)
batch$summary[, c("document_id", "measure_id", "weighting", "estimate")]
#>   document_id  measure_id weighting estimate
#> 1          d1 familiarity     token      5.5
#> 2          d1 familiarity      type      5.5
#> 3          d1         aoa     token      4.6
#> 4          d1         aoa      type      4.6
#> 5          d2 familiarity     token       NA
#> 6          d2 familiarity      type       NA
#> 7          d2         aoa     token     11.5
#> 8          d2         aoa      type     11.5
